note: Every model the workbench runs is listed here with the SHA-256 of its weights. A file whose hash does not match is refused. Models are shipped in this package so the workbench runs with no network access.

models.task: Single-image super resolution of the luma channel, 2x
models.architecture: FSRCNN (8 convolutional layers, PReLU, sub-pixel output)
models.reference: C. Dong, C. C. Loy and X. Tang, 'Accelerating the Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network', ECCV 2016.
models.source: https://github.com/Saafke/FSRCNN_Tensorflow models/FSRCNN_x2.pb (SHA-256 366b33f0084c7b3f2bf6724f0a2c77bca94fcec9d7b6d72389d330073b380d5c), converted to ONNX with tools/convert_sr_models.py; weights unchanged
models.training_data: The FSRCNN paper trains on the 91-image set and General-100 with bicubic down-sampling; the source repository does not document its exact training run.
models.limits: Learned from natural photographs: predicts plausible detail, which was not necessarily recorded. Trained on bicubic down-sampling, so it fits CCTV compression and blur poorly.

models.task: Single-image super resolution of colour images, 4x, robust to blur, noise and JPEG compression
models.architecture: RRDBNet (ESRGAN generator, 23 residual-in-residual dense blocks, 16.7M parameters) trained adversarially
models.source: https://github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN/releases/download/v0.1.0/RealESRGAN_x4plus.pth (SHA-256 4fa0d38905f75ac06eb49a7951b426670021be3018265fd191d2125df9d682f1), converted to ONNX with tools/convert_realesrgan.py; weights unchanged
models.limits: Trained with an adversarial loss to produce sharp, natural-looking texture: it invents detail, including plausible but wrong characters, faces and texture. Its output is an investigative aid only and must never be read as recorded detail.
models.reference: X. Wang, L. Xie, C. Dong and Y. Shan, 'Real-ESRGAN: Training Real-World Blind Super-Resolution with Pure Synthetic Data', ICCV Workshops 2021.
models.training_data: DIV2K, Flickr2K and OutdoorSceneTraining photographs, degraded on the fly with a synthetic second-order model of real cameras: blur, resizing, sensor noise and JPEG compression (per the paper).

models.task: Single-image super resolution of colour images, 4x (small, fast model)
models.architecture: SRVGGNetCompact (32 plain 3x3 convolutions with PReLU, sub-pixel output; 1.2M parameters) trained adversarially
models.source: https://github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN/releases/download/v0.2.5.0/realesr-general-x4v3.pth (SHA-256 8dc7edb9ac80ccdc30c3a5dca6616509367f05fbc184ad95b731f05bece96292), converted to ONNX with tools/convert_realesrgan.py; weights unchanged
models.limits: As for sr.realesrgan_x4plus, with less capacity: fewer invented textures but weaker on heavy compression.
models.reference: X. Wang, L. Xie, C. Dong and Y. Shan, 'Real-ESRGAN: Training Real-World Blind Super-Resolution with Pure Synthetic Data', ICCV Workshops 2021.
models.training_data: DIV2K, Flickr2K and OutdoorSceneTraining photographs, degraded on the fly with a synthetic second-order model of real cameras: blur, resizing, sensor noise and JPEG compression (per the paper).

models.task: Face detection with five landmarks (eyes, nose tip, mouth corners)
models.reference: W. Wu, H. Peng and S. Yu, 'YuNet: A Tiny Millisecond-level Face Detector', Machine Intelligence Research 20, 2023.
models.limits: Detects faces of roughly 10 to 300 pixels; misses profile, occluded and very small faces. A miss is not evidence that no face is present.

models.task: Probability that a whole image was generated by a generative model (diffusion, GAN or other)
models.architecture: ViT-Small/16 at 384x384 (timm vit_small_patch16_384) with a one-logit head
models.reference: J. Park and A. Owens, 'Community Forensics: Using Thousands of Generators to Train Fake Image Detectors', CVPR 2025 (arXiv 2411.04125).
models.source: https://huggingface.co/OwensLab/commfor-model-384 model.safetensors (SHA-256 b89f36275f3bf5e2b040eee36597a8f19db051bff9a473a9cf7b2466284fb387), converted to ONNX with tools/convert_commfor.py; weights unchanged. The converted model reproduces the authors' published scores on their example images to within 4e-6.
models.training_data: Community Forensics: 2.7 million generated images from about 4,800 generators (mostly latent-diffusion models and fine-tunes from Hugging Face, plus GANs, pixel-diffusion and commercial models) paired with 2.7 million real images (LAION, ImageNet, COCO, FFHQ, CelebA, MetFaces, AFHQ, Forchheim, IMD2020, Landscapes HQ, VISION).
models.validation: Authors: mAP 0.991, accuracy 0.925 on their 26K-image evaluation set of 21 generators unseen in training (11 commercial). Lucida's own measurement is in the synthetic.generated detector card.
models.limits: Scores whole images: not built to localise a generated region pasted into a real photo. Training data is mostly latent diffusion; GANs, autoregressive and post-2024 generators are under-represented. The authors state its error rates are still too high for consequential use on its own.
